mainTopic: Sanhedrin 88a: The disputes behind the משנה's categories for a זקן ממרא, and when he is executed (tradition against reasoning: רב כהנא and רבי אלעזר)
overview: The גמרא goes through the words of the משנה about a זקן ממרא, an elder who rules against the בית דין הגדול. For each word it shows a real מחלוקת he could rule on. It finishes the נגעים example: רבי יונתן בן אבטולמוס learns from a גזירה שוה that a garment fully covered by a נגע is טהור. 'דברי' means ערכין, חרמים and הקדשות, each tied to a known dispute. 'ריבות' means סוטה, עגלה ערופה and טהרת מצורע, and 'בשעריך' means לקט, שכחה and פיאה, and each of these is also tied to a known dispute. Then the גמרא turns to the three courts. רב כהנא says the זקן is killed only when he relies on his own reasoning against the court's tradition, and he proves it from עקביא בן מהללאל. רבי אלעזר says that even a זקן with a tradition is killed, to keep disputes from spreading. He explains that עקביא was spared because he never gave a practical ruling. A proof from the משנה's wording is pushed aside, and a new proof from רבי יאשיה's three teachings begins and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Where do we learn that a garment fully covered by a נגע is pure?
steps.stepSummary: The end of רבי יונתן בן אבטולמוס's question: what is the source that when a נגע spreads over an entire garment, the garment is טהור?
steps.simpleTranslation: ...that if a נגע spreads over a whole garment, the garment is pure?
steps.whatsHappening: We are in the middle of a question that began before this section. The question asks for a source that a garment completely covered by a נגע becomes pure, and the answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a person, the תורה says that if a נגע covers the whole body he is טהור. The question is whether the same surprising rule applies to garments, and where that would come from. This is one example of a נגע dispute that a זקן ממרא could rule on.

keyTerms.meaning: Spreading out; here, the נגע spreading over the entire item
Garments; clothing that can get a נגע
Pure; not טמא

phrases.english: for a spreading in garments, that it is pure?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the question that began in the text right before this section.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that a garment fully covered by a נגע is טהור.

steps.title: Learning garments from people through matching words
steps.stepSummary: The words קרחת and גבחת appear both for a person's נגע and for a garment's נגע. So, just as a person fully covered is טהור, a garment fully covered is טהור.
steps.simpleTranslation: The words 'קרחת' and 'גבחת' are said about a person, and the words 'קרחת' and 'גבחת' are said about garments. Just as there, if it spread over all of him he is pure, so too here, if it spread over all of it, it is pure.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יונתן בן אבטולמוס answers with a גזירה שוה, a link made through the same words appearing in two places in the תורה. The rule for people is carried over to garments.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the same pair of words is used in both places, the two kinds of נגע share this rule: covering the whole thing makes it pure. The רבנן disagree, so a person who touches such a garment and enters the מקדש would be חייב כרת according to them but not according to רבי יונתן. That is why this is a real case for a זקן ממרא.

keyTerms.meaning: Baldness at the back of the head; for garments, the old, worn side of the cloth
Baldness at the front of the head; for garments, the new side of the cloth
Just as there... so too here; the formula for carrying a rule from one case to another
It spread over the whole of it

steps.whatToRemember: A נגע that covers an entire garment makes it טהור according to רבי יונתן בן אבטולמוס, learned from the rule for people. This is one example of a נגע dispute that could make someone a זקן ממרא.

phrases.english: 'Karachat' and 'gabachat' are stated regarding a person,
and 'karachat' and 'gabachat' are stated regarding garments.
Just as there, if it spread over all of him, he is pure,
phrases.notes: 'There' means a person: if the נגע covers his whole body, he is pure.

phrases.english: so too here, if it spread over all of it, it is pure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 1.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גזירה שוה from the shared words קרחת and גבחת makes garments follow the rule for people: fully covered means טהור.

steps.title: What the word 'דברי' in the משנה refers to
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the משנה's word 'דברי' means ערכין, חרמים and הקדשות.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Matters of': these are valuations, dedications and consecrations.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the next word in the פסוק the משנה uses, 'דברי', and says which three areas it covers. This is a setup line: the next steps give the dispute for each area.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A new set of topics opens here: vows that give money or property to the מקדש. The גמרא will now show a real מחלוקת in each area that a זקן ממרא could rule against.

keyTerms.meaning: Valuations; pledging the fixed תורה value of a person to the מקדש
Dedications; property declared חרם
Consecrations; items made הקדש

phrases.english: 'Matters of': these are the valuations,
and the dedications, and the consecrations.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from נגעים to the next word of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'דברי' refers to ערכין, חרמים and הקדשות.

steps.title: The ערכין dispute: valuing a baby under one month
steps.stepSummary: For ערכין, the case is the מחלוקת between רבי מאיר and חכמים about someone who pledges the ערך of a baby less than a month old.
steps.simpleTranslation: Valuations: this is the dispute of רבי מאיר and the רבנן, as we learned: someone who pledges the valuation of a child under one month old. רבי מאיר says he gives the child's monetary worth. The חכמים say he said nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the example for ערכין. It points to a known מחלוקת about a ערך pledge for a baby the תורה gives no ערך to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה lists ערכין only from one month old. רבי מאיר says a person does not speak for nothing, so he meant to give the baby's worth as a gift. The חכמים say his words have no effect, so the money stays חולין. That changes whether the money is הקדש, which can lead to serious results such as whether a קידושין done with it works.

keyTerms.meaning: One who pledges a person's ערך
Less than one month old
He gives his monetary worth (what he would sell for)
He said nothing; his words have no effect
A dispute

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up ערך and דמים. A ערך is the fixed amount the תורה sets by age and gender. דמים is what the person would actually be worth on the market. רבי מאיר turns a pledge that cannot work as a ערך into a pledge of דמים.

phrases.english: Valuations: in the dispute of Rabbi Meir and the Rabbis,
as we learned: one who valuates a child less than a month old,
Rabbi Meir says: he gives his monetary worth,
and the Rabbis say: he did not say anything.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fills in the first of the three categories listed in step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ערכין case for a זקן ממרא is the dispute over pledging the ערך of a baby under one month: רבי מאיר says he pays its worth, the חכמים say his words do nothing.

steps.title: The חרמים dispute: where unspecified חרמים go
steps.stepSummary: For חרמים, the case is the מחלוקת of רבי יהודה בן בתירה and the רבנן. רבי יהודה בן בתירה says an unspecified חרם goes to בדק הבית, based on a פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: Dedications: this is the dispute of רבי יהודה בן בתירה and the רבנן, as we learned: רבי יהודה בן בתירה says unspecified dedications go to the upkeep of the מקדש, as it says: 'Every dedicated item is most holy to ה׳.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the example for חרמים. It starts quoting a משנה where רבי יהודה בן בתירה says that a חרם given without saying its purpose goes to the מקדש building fund. The next step gives the other side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה בן בתירה reads 'קדש קדשים הוא לה׳' to mean the חרם belongs to the מקדש itself, which is בדק הבית. The רבנן, whose view comes in the next step, say an unspecified חרם goes to the כהנים. If it is הקדש it is forbidden to use, but if it belongs to a כהן it is ordinary property, so the dispute has serious results.

keyTerms.meaning: Dedications made without saying what they are for
The fund for the upkeep and repair of the מקדש
An item declared dedicated
Most holy

steps.whyThisMatters: Whether an unspecified חרם is הקדש or belongs to the כהנים decides if using it is מעילה or allowed. That makes it a real case where a זקן ממרא's ruling would matter.

phrases.aramaic: הַחֲרָמִים – בִּפְלוּגְתָּא דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בְּתִירָה וְרַבָּנַן.
phrases.english: Dedications: in the dispute of Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira and the Rabbis.

phrases.aramaic: דִּתְנַן, רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בְּתִירָה אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: As we learned: Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira says:
Unspecified dedications are for Temple maintenance,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״כׇּל חֵרֶם קֹדֶשׁ קֳדָשִׁים הוּא לַה׳״.
phrases.english: as it is stated: 'Every dedicated item is most holy to the Lord.'

steps.triggerLanguage: הַחֲרָמִים – בִּפְלוּגְתָּא דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בְּתִירָה וְרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fills in the second of the three categories listed in step 3, after ערכין.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The חרמים case for a זקן ממרא is the dispute over unspecified חרמים: רבי יהודה בן בתירה says they go to בדק הבית, learned from ויקרא 27:28.

steps.title: The Sages say an unspecified חרם goes to the כהן
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים argue with רבי יהודה בן בתירה. They hold that an unspecified חרם goes to the כהנים, based on a פסוק about a dedicated field.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the Sages say: unspecified dedications go to the כהן, because the פסוק says, 'Like a dedicated field, to the כהן shall be its possession.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the חרמים dispute from step 5 by giving the other side: the חכמים say an unspecified חרם goes to the כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה בן בתירה said an unspecified חרם goes to בדק הבית. The חכמים disagree and bring their own פסוק. That פסוק says a dedicated field belongs to the כהן, so they learn that every unspecified חרם goes to the כהן.

keyTerms.meaning: Dedications where the person did not say what they are for
A priest
A dedicated field
A possession or property

phrases.english: And the Sages say:
Unspecified dedications go to the priest,
as it is said: "Like a dedicated field,
to the priest shall be its possession."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view to רבי יהודה בן בתירה in the same dispute
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the חכמים, an unspecified חרם goes to the כהנים.

steps.title: Then what does 'most holy to ה׳' teach?
steps.stepSummary: If an unspecified חרם goes to the כהן, why does the פסוק call a חרם 'most holy to ה׳', which sounds like it belongs to הקדש?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why does the פסוק say, 'It is most holy to ה׳'?
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים's view is being challenged with the פסוק that רבי יהודה בן בתירה used. This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'most holy to ה׳' sound like the חרם goes to ה׳, meaning בדק הבית. If the חכמים say it goes to the כהן, those words seem to have no job. The question demands a purpose for them.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
Why does the פסוק need to say this?
Most holy

phrases.english: If so, why does the verse say:
"It is most holy to the Lord"?
phrases.notes: ויקרא 27:28. This is the same פסוק רבי יהודה בן בתירה used for his view.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the חכמים using their opponent's פסוק
steps.kashyaTarget: The חכמים's view that an unspecified חרם goes to the כהן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק calls a חרם 'most holy to ה׳', which suggests הקדש. If it goes to the כהן, those words seem pointless.

steps.title: It teaches that חרם can apply to any קרבן
steps.stepSummary: The words teach a different law: a חרם can take effect on offerings, both קדשי קדשים and קדשים קלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: It teaches that a חרם takes effect on most-holy offerings and on offerings of lesser holiness.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים answer that the words 'most holy to ה׳' teach that a person can make a חרם even on something that is already a קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים give the פסוק a different job. It does not say where the חרם goes. It teaches that a חרם can take effect even on items that are already holy, whether קדשי קדשים or קדשים קלים. So their rule that an unspecified חרם goes to the כהן still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Takes effect
Offerings of the highest holiness
Offerings of lesser holiness

phrases.english: That it takes effect on offerings of the most sacred order
and on offerings of lesser sanctity.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁחָל עַל קׇדְשֵׁי קָדָשִׁים וְעַל קָדָשִׁים קַלִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by giving the פסוק a different purpose
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigns the פסוק to teach a different law
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The words 'most holy to ה׳' seemed to teach that a חרם goes to הקדש.
steps.terutzMaskana: The words teach that a חרם can take effect on both kinds of offerings, so the חכמים's rule still stands.
steps.whatToRemember: חרמים dispute: רבי יהודה בן בתירה says an unspecified חרם goes to בדק הבית. The חכמים say it goes to the כהן, and they read 'most holy' as teaching that a חרם can apply to offerings.

steps.title: The הקדשות case: how many people are needed to redeem הקדש
steps.stepSummary: For הקדשות, the case is the dispute between רבי אליעזר בן יעקב and the רבנן. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says even a tiny item of הקדש needs ten people to redeem it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Consecrations: this is the dispute between רבי אליעזר בן יעקב and the Rabbis. As a ברייתא teaches: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says, even a small fork of הקדש needs ten people to redeem it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the third example of 'דברי', which is הקדשות. It names the dispute it means and quotes a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To redeem הקדש, it has to be valued by a group of people. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says even something tiny needs ten people. The text quotes only his side; the רבנן are understood to disagree and require fewer.

keyTerms.meaning: Things consecrated to the בית המקדש
In the dispute of
A small fork or hook, something of very little value
To redeem it, meaning to take it out of הקדש

steps.confusionAlert: Only רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's side is written here. The רבנן's view is not quoted in this text, but they disagree with him.

phrases.english: Consecrations: in the dispute
of Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya'akov and the Rabbis.

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא, רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: As it is taught: Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya'akov says:
Even a small fork of consecrated property
requires ten people to redeem it.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֶקְדֵּשׁוֹת, בִּפְלוּגְתָּא דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב וְרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the second example (חרמים) to the third (הקדשות) in the list from step 3
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, redeeming any הקדש, even something tiny, requires ten people.

steps.title: What 'ריבות' means: three cases
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the משנה's word 'ריבות' as השקאת סוטה, עריפת העגלה, and טהרת מצורע.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Disputes' means giving the סוטה the water to drink, breaking the neck of the calf, and purifying a מצורע.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next word in the משנה, 'ריבות', and lists the three topics it refers to. This sets up a separate explanation of each one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just as 'דברי' meant three topics, 'ריבות' also means three. Each one will be tied to a known dispute between תנאים, starting with סוטה in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Disputes, a word from the פסוק quoted in the משנה
Making a סוטה drink the bitter water
Breaking the neck of the calf when a dead body is found and the killer is unknown
The purification process for a מצורע

phrases.english: "Disputes": this is giving the bitter waters to a sota to drink,
and the heifer whose neck is broken, and the purification of a leper.

steps.triggerLanguage: ״רִיבֹת״ – זֶה הַשְׁקָאַת סוֹטָה, וַעֲרִיפַת הָעֶגְלָה, וְטׇהֳרַת מְצוֹרָע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes 'דברי' and starts explaining the next word of the משנה, 'ריבות'
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'ריבות' refers to השקאת סוטה, עריפת העגלה, and טהרת מצורע.

steps.title: The סוטה case: רבי אליעזר's view
steps.stepSummary: For השקאת סוטה, the case is the dispute between רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע. רבי אליעזר says the warning needs two witnesses, but the drinking can happen based on one witness or the husband alone.
steps.simpleTranslation: Giving the סוטה to drink: this is the dispute between רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע. As the משנה teaches: about one who warns his wife, רבי אליעזר says he warns her in front of two witnesses, and he makes her drink based on one witness or even based on himself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the first 'ריבות' case by naming a dispute and quoting the משנה. This step gives רבי אליעזר's side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A סוטה process has two stages: the husband warns her not to be alone with a certain man, and then, if she was alone with him, he brings her to drink. רבי אליעזר says the warning needs two witnesses. For the seclusion, one witness, or even just the husband, is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: One who warns his wife not to be alone with a certain man
Makes her drink the bitter water
One witness
Based on himself, the husband's own word

phrases.english: Giving the bitter waters to a sota to drink: in the dispute
of Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Yehoshua,
as we learned: One who warns his wife,

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: מְקַנֵּא עַל פִּי שְׁנַיִם,
phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says: He warns her based on two witnesses,
and gives her to drink based on one witness
or based on himself.
phrases.notes: The 'one witness' or the husband here is someone who saw her go off alone with the man after the warning.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַשְׁקָאַת סוֹטָה – בִּפְלוּגְתָּא דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the first of the three 'ריבות' cases listed in step 10
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי אליעזר, the warning needs two witnesses, but the drinking can be based on one witness or the husband himself.

steps.title: The סוטה case: רבי יהושע's view
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע says both the warning and the drinking need two witnesses.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע says: he warns her in front of two witnesses, and he makes her drink only based on two witnesses.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the משנה with רבי יהושע's side of the סוטה dispute.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע agrees the warning needs two witnesses. He disagrees about the seclusion: one witness is not enough, and two are needed before she can be made to drink. So if only one witness saw the seclusion, the two תנאים reach different results.

keyTerms.meaning: Two, meaning two witnesses

steps.whatToRemember: סוטה dispute: both agree the warning needs two witnesses. רבי אליעזר says the drinking can be based on one witness, while רבי יהושע requires two.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר: מְקַנֵּא עַל פִּי שְׁנַיִם,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua says: He warns her based on two witnesses,
and gives her to drink based on two witnesses.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר: מְקַנֵּא עַל פִּי שְׁנַיִם, וּמַשְׁקֶה עַל פִּי שְׁנַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view in the same סוטה dispute
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהושע, both the warning and the drinking require two witnesses.

steps.title: The dispute about measuring for the heifer
steps.stepSummary: For עריפת עגלה, the case in mind is the dispute between רבי אליעזר and רבי עקיבא about where on the dead body the measuring starts.
steps.simpleTranslation: The heifer whose neck is broken: this is the dispute between רבי אליעזר and רבי עקיבא. As we learned in a משנה: From where on the body did they measure? רבי אליעזר says: from his navel. רבי עקיבא says: from his nose. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says: from the place where he became a slain person, from his neck.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the second item of ריבות, עריפת עגלה. It shows the real disagreement a זקן ממרא could argue about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a dead body is found, we measure to the nearest city, and that city brings the עגלה ערופה. The תנאים argue about which point on the body we measure from. Since each view could pick a different city, this argument has real legal results.

keyTerms.meaning: Breaking the neck of a heifer when a murder victim is found and the killer is unknown
They measure (the distance to the nearest city)
His navel
His nose
A slain person

phrases.english: The heifer whose neck is broken:
this is in the dispute of Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Akiva.
As we learned in a mishna: From where would they measure?
phrases.notes: He means from which spot on the dead body they start measuring to find the closest city.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says: from his navel.
Rabbi Akiva says: from his nose.
Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya'akov says:
from the place where he became a slain person, from his neck.

steps.triggerLanguage: עריפת עגלה בפלוגתא דרבי אליעזר ורבי עקיבא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After השקאת סוטה (steps 11 and 12), the גמרא moves to the second item listed under ריבות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The dispute about עריפת עגלה is where the measuring starts: navel (רבי אליעזר), nose (רבי עקיבא), or neck (רבי אליעזר בן יעקב).

steps.title: The dispute about a leper missing a body part
steps.stepSummary: For טהרת מצורע, the case in mind is the dispute between רבי שמעון and the רבנן about a מצורע who lacks a right thumb, big toe or ear.
steps.simpleTranslation: The purification of a leper: this is the dispute between רבי שמעון and the רבנן. As we learned in a משנה: If he has no thumb, no big toe, or no right ear, he can never become pure. רבי אליעזר says: the כהן puts it on the place where the body part would be, and that is enough. רבי שמעון says: he puts it on the left one, and that is enough.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the third item of ריבות, טהרת מצורע. It points to an argument over whether a מצורע missing a body part can ever become pure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To purify a מצורע, the כהן puts blood and oil on his right thumb, right big toe and right ear. The first view in the משנה says that without these he can never become pure. רבי אליעזר and רבי שמעון each find a way for him to become pure, so the outcome is very different.

keyTerms.meaning: The purification process of a person with צרעת
Thumb
Big toe
Purity ever (here: never able to become pure)
And he has done his obligation

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא names the dispute as רבי שמעון against the רבנן, but the משנה also brings רבי אליעזר. Both רבי אליעזר and רבי שמעון let him become pure. The רבנן are the first, unnamed view, who say he never can.

phrases.english: The purification of a leper:
this is in the dispute of Rabbi Shimon and the Rabbis.
As we learned in a mishna: If he has no thumb,
big toe, or right ear,
he can never become pure.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: נוֹתֵן לוֹ עַל מְקוֹמוֹ וְיוֹצֵא.
phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says: He places it for him on its place, and he has done his obligation.
phrases.notes: "It" is the blood and oil. "Its place" is the spot where the missing body part would have been.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: נוֹתֵן עַל שֶׁל שְׂמֹאל וְיוֹצֵא.
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says: He places it on the left one, and he has done his obligation.

steps.triggerLanguage: טהרת מצורע בפלוגתא דרבי שמעון ורבנן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This continues the list from step 10 and gives the third item of ריבות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The dispute about טהרת מצורע is whether a מצורע missing a right thumb, big toe or ear can ever become pure.

steps.title: Explaining 'in your gates': gleanings and forgotten sheaves
steps.stepSummary: The משנה's word בשעריך means לקט, שכחה and פאה. For לקט and שכחה, two count as gifts for the poor and three do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: "In your gates": this means gleanings, forgotten sheaves and the corner of the field. Gleanings: as we learned in a משנה, two stalks are gleanings, three are not. Forgotten sheaves: two sheaves are forgotten sheaves, three are not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the next word in the משנה, בשעריך. It says the word refers to the gifts for the poor, and it shows the disputed cases for לקט and שכחה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Stalks that fall during harvest (לקט) and sheaves the owner forgets (שכחה) belong to the poor. This משנה sets a limit: two count as a gift for the poor, but three stay with the owner. This number is where the argument in the next step comes in.

keyTerms.meaning: In your gates (the word in the משנה and the פסוק)
Gleanings: stalks that fall during harvest and go to the poor
Forgotten sheaves left in the field for the poor
The corner of the field left for the poor
Stalks of grain
Sheaves (bundles of grain)

phrases.english: "In your gates":
this is gleanings, forgotten sheaves, and the corner of the field.
Gleanings: as we learned in a mishna:
two stalks are gleanings,
three are not gleanings.
Forgotten sheaves: two sheaves are forgotten sheaves,
three are not forgotten sheaves.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The list of ריבות is finished, so the גמרא moves on to explain the next word in the משנה, בשעריך.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בשעריך means the gifts for the poor. In the anonymous view, two stalks or sheaves go to the poor and three do not.

steps.title: בית שמאי give three to the poor
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי disagree about all these cases: three go to the poor, and only four belong to the owner.
steps.simpleTranslation: About all of them, בית שמאי say: three go to the poor, and four go to the owner.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the משנה with the view of בית שמאי. This shows that there is a real disagreement about the case of three.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first view in the previous step says three stalks or sheaves stay with the owner. בית שמאי say three still go to the poor, and only four go to the owner. So the case of three is where the two views argue, and the answer decides who owns the grain.

keyTerms.meaning: The students and school of שמאי
To the poor person
The owner of the field

steps.whatToRemember: For לקט and שכחה, the dispute is about the case of three: the first view gives three to the owner, while בית שמאי give three to the poor.

phrases.english: And about all of them, Beit Shammai say:
three go to the poor person, and four go to the owner.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This finishes the quote from the משנה in step 15 by bringing the other view, so the dispute becomes clear.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית שמאי: three stalks or sheaves go to the poor, and four go to the owner.

steps.title: Which dispute about פיאה the משנה means
steps.stepSummary: For פיאה, the case in mind is the dispute between רבי ישמעאל and the רבנן. The רבנן's side is quoted: פיאה can be separated from standing grain, from sheaves, or from the pile, but not later.
steps.simpleTranslation: For פיאה, the case is the dispute of רבי ישמעאל and the רבנן. We learned: the best way to do פיאה is to separate it from grain still standing in the field. If he didn't, he separates it from the sheaves. If he didn't do that either, he separates it from the grain pile, as long as he has not yet smoothed it. If he already smoothed it, he first takes off the tithes and then gives the פיאה to the poor man.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues explaining which disputes about the משנה's word בשעריך can make a זקן ממרא. Now it gives the dispute for פיאה. It quotes a source that lists the latest stages when פיאה can still be given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן's list stops at the grain pile, so after that stage there is no more פיאה. This sets up רבי ישמעאל's opinion in the next step, which adds one more stage. A זקן who argues on this point about a matter of the poor could become a זקן ממרא.

keyTerms.meaning: The corner of the field left for the poor
Grain still standing, attached to the ground
Sheaves: bundles of cut grain
The pile of threshed grain kernels
He smoothed the pile, the final step of processing the grain

phrases.english: פיאה: in the dispute of רבי ישמעאל and the Rabbis.

phrases.aramaic: דִּתְנַן: מִצְוַת פֵּיאָה לְהַפְרִישׁ מִן הַקָּמָה.
phrases.english: As we learned: the mitzva of פיאה is to separate it from the standing grain.

phrases.aramaic: לֹא הִפְרִישׁ מִן הַקָּמָה – יַפְרִישׁ מִן הָעֳמָרִין.
phrases.english: If he did not separate it from the standing grain, he separates it from the sheaves.

phrases.aramaic: לֹא הִפְרִישׁ מִן הָעֳמָרִין – יַפְרִישׁ מִן הַכְּרִי
phrases.english: If he did not separate it from the sheaves, he separates it from the grain pile
as long as he has not yet smoothed it.
phrases.notes: Smoothing the pile is the last step of processing, and it is the point where tithes become required.

phrases.english: If he smoothed it, he tithes and gives to him.
phrases.notes: 'To him' means to the poor person who gets the פיאה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of disputes covered by בשעריך, after לקט and שכחה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the רבנן, פיאה can be separated at the latest from the grain pile. If the pile was already smoothed, he tithes first and then gives the פיאה.

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל: פיאה even from the dough
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל holds that פיאה can be separated even after the grain became dough.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the name of רבי ישמעאל they said: he separates פיאה even from the dough.
steps.whatsHappening: Now we hear the other side of the dispute. רבי ישמעאל extends פיאה one stage further than the רבנן do.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the רבנן, once the grain is ground and made into dough there is no more פיאה. For רבי ישמעאל, the obligation still applies. So a piece of dough given to a poor man is real פיאה for רבי ישמעאל but not for the רבנן. That is the kind of disagreement over 'matters of the gate' the משנה means.

keyTerms.meaning: Dough
In the name of

steps.whatToRemember: The three cases of בשעריך are לקט, שכחה and פיאה. Each one points to a known dispute about what really counts as a gift to the poor.

phrases.english: In the name of רבי ישמעאל they said:
He separates it even from the dough.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing opinion in the dispute introduced in step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי ישמעאל, פיאה can be separated even from the dough.

steps.title: Both sides quote tradition: not killed
steps.stepSummary: Back to the משנה about the three courts. רב כהנא says that if both the זקן and the court base themselves on tradition, the זקן is not killed.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'three courts' and so on. רב כהנא said: if he says his view comes from a tradition, and they say theirs comes from a tradition, he is not killed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה, about the three courts in ירושלים where the זקן ממרא is judged. רב כהנא begins explaining when the זקן is actually put to death.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here both sides have a received teaching, so the זקן is not rebelling against the חכמים. He is following what his own teachers handed down. Two traditions disagreeing is not rebellion.

keyTerms.meaning: From a received tradition, passed down from one's teachers
He is not executed
Courts
A rebellious elder who rules against the Great Court

phrases.english: Three courts, etc.
phrases.notes: The גמרא is quoting the start of a line in the משנה: the three courts in ירושלים where the זקן comes.

phrases.english: רב כהנא said:
If he says it is from tradition,
phrases.notes: 'He' is the זקן ממרא; 'they' in the next line are the judges of the court.

phrases.english: and they say it is from tradition,
he is not executed.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁלֹשָׁה בָּתֵּי דִינִין וְכוּ׳. אָמַר רַב כָּהֲנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the list of disputes and turns to a new line of the משנה about the court process.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When both the זקן and the court rely on tradition, the זקן is not executed.

steps.title: Reasoning against reasoning, or tradition against reasoning: not killed
steps.stepSummary: If both sides rely on their own reasoning, he is not killed. If he has a tradition and they only have reasoning, he is surely not killed.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he says 'this is how I see it' and they say 'this is how we see it,' he is not killed. And all the more so, if he says 'from tradition' and they say 'this is how we see it,' he is not killed.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא goes through more combinations of how each side backs up its view. In each of these cases the זקן is not executed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When both sides only use reasoning, his reasoning is as good as theirs, so it is not rebellion. When he has a tradition and they only have reasoning, his position is even stronger, so it is a כל שכן (all the more so) that he is not killed.

keyTerms.meaning: This is how it looks to me; my own reasoning
And all the more so

phrases.english: If he says: 'This is how it is in my eyes,'

phrases.aramaic: וְהֵן אוֹמְרִין: ״כָּךְ הוּא בְּעֵינֵינוּ״ – אֵינוֹ נֶהֱרָג.
phrases.english: and they say: 'This is how it is in our eyes,' he is not executed.
And all the more so if he says: 'From tradition,'

phrases.aramaic: וְהֵן אוֹמְרִין: ״כָּךְ הוּא בְּעֵינֵינוּ״ – אֵינוֹ נֶהֱרָג.
phrases.english: and they say: 'This is how it is in our eyes,' he is not executed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רב כהנא's list of combinations after the tradition-against-tradition case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When both sides use reasoning, or when he has tradition against their reasoning, he is not executed.

steps.title: The only case he is killed: his reasoning against their tradition
steps.stepSummary: He is killed only when he relies on his own reasoning and the court holds a received tradition.
steps.simpleTranslation: He is not killed unless he says 'this is how I see it' and they say 'we have it from tradition.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא now gives the one case where the זקן ממרא is executed. This finishes his rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The only case left is the weakest one for the זקן: his own opinion against a tradition the court received. Ruling against a handed-down tradition with nothing but his own view is true rebellion, so only here is he killed.

keyTerms.meaning: Unless he says; only when he says

steps.whatToRemember: A זקן ממרא is executed only for 'my reasoning' against the court's 'tradition.' In every other combination he is not executed.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the sides. It is the court that must have the tradition, and the זקן who has only his own reasoning. If the זקן has the tradition, he is never killed.

phrases.english: Not until he says: 'This is how it is in my eyes,'
and they say: 'From tradition.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב כהנא's list by naming the single case of execution.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A זקן ממרא is executed only when he relies on his own reasoning against the court's received tradition.

steps.title: Proof from עקביא בן מהללאל
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא proves his rule: עקביא בן מהללאל argued against the חכמים and was still not killed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Know that this is true, because they did not kill עקביא בן מהללאל.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא brings a proof from history. עקביא בן מהללאל held firm against the חכמים, yet he was not put to death.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If every elder who argued with the court were killed, עקביא should have been killed. He was not. This shows that someone holding a tradition from his teachers is not a זקן ממרא, which supports רב כהנא's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Know that it is so; a phrase that introduces a proof

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the death penalty of זקן ממרא is not about disagreeing in itself. It is about setting one's own opinion against a received tradition.

phrases.english: Know that it is so, for

phrases.aramaic: לֹא הָרְגוּ אֶת עֲקַבְיָא בֶּן מַהֲלַלְאֵל.
phrases.english: they did not execute עקביא בן מהללאל.
phrases.notes: The proof assumes עקביא was holding on to what he received from his teachers, so his case fits 'tradition' on his side.

steps.triggerLanguage: תֵּדַע, שֶׁהֲרֵי לֹא הָרְגוּ אֶת עֲקַבְיָא בֶּן מַהֲלַלְאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב כהנא's rule with a historical case.
steps.raayaObject: רב כהנא's rule that a זקן who relies on tradition is not executed.
steps.raayaSupportSource: עקביא בן מהללאל disagreed with the חכמים but was not executed.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: Even a זקן With a Tradition Is Killed
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר holds that even if the זקן says he has a tradition and the court only has reasoning, he is still killed, so that disputes will not multiply.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר says: Even if the elder says his view comes from a received tradition, and the court says 'this is how it looks to us,' he is killed. This is so that arguments will not spread in Israel.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second opinion, from רבי אלעזר, that argues with רב כהנא's rule from the previous steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב כהנא said a זקן with a tradition is never killed. רבי אלעזר disagrees: what counts is keeping one clear ruling for all of ישראל, not who has the stronger source. So even a זקן with a tradition is killed if he goes against the court.

keyTerms.meaning: From what was heard, meaning a tradition passed down from teachers
This is how it seems in our eyes, meaning a view based on our own reasoning
He is killed (executed)
Disputes, disagreements

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows two different ideas behind the זקן ממרא law: respecting the strongest source (רב כהנא) versus keeping the nation united under one ruling (רבי אלעזר).

phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar says:
Even if he says, "It is from a tradition,"
and they say, "This is how it seems in our eyes" —
he is killed,
so that disputes will not multiply in Israel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an opposing opinion to רב כהנא's rule (steps 19-21).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A זקן who holds a tradition against the court's reasoning is still killed, to prevent disputes in ישראל.

steps.title: Why עקביא בן מהללאל Was Not Killed
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר answers רב כהנא's proof: עקביא בן מהללאל was not killed because he never ruled for actual practice.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you ask: Why did they not kill עקביא בן מהללאל? Because he did not rule the law for people to actually follow.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר expects the question from עקביא בן מהללאל (step 22) and answers it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב כהנא used עקביא as proof that a זקן with a tradition is not killed. רבי אלעזר says that is not the reason. עקביא only argued in learning and never told people to act against the court, and a זקן ממרא is killed only for a practical ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: He ruled, gave a halachic decision
Law for actual practice, telling people what to do

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי אלעזר says עקביא was right. He only says עקביא's case does not prove anything, because he never gave a practical ruling.

phrases.english: And if you will say:
For what reason did they not kill
Akavya ben Mahalalel?
phrases.notes: This is the case רב כהנא brought as his proof in step 22.

phrases.english: Because he did not rule the law for actual practice.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם תֹּאמַר: מִפְּנֵי מָה לֹא הָרְגוּ אֶת עֲקַבְיָא בֶּן מַהֲלַלְאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends רבי אלעזר's view against the עקביא proof that רב כהנא brought.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case: עקביא never gave a practical ruling.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: עקביא was not killed because he held a tradition, which proves רב כהנא's rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: עקביא was not killed only because he never ruled for practice, so the case fits רבי אלעזר too.

steps.title: Trying to Prove רבי אלעזר From the משנה's Words
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the משנה's wording, 'this is how I taught and this is how my colleagues taught,' covers a זקן with a tradition against the court's reasoning.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: 'This is how I explained, and this is how my colleagues explained; this is how I taught, and this is how my colleagues taught.' Isn't this talking about a case where he says 'from tradition' and they say 'this is how it seems to us'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to support רבי אלעזר from the words the זקן says in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'this is how I taught' sounds like the זקן is repeating something he received. If the משנה still says he is killed, a זקן with a tradition can be killed, as רבי אלעזר says and against רב כהנא.

keyTerms.meaning: I expounded, explained from the verses
I taught
Isn't it that... (introduces a suggested reading)

phrases.aramaic: תְּנַן: כָּךְ דָּרַשְׁתִּי, וְכָךְ דָּרְשׁוּ חֲבֵירַי;
phrases.english: We learned: This is how I expounded, and that is how my colleagues expounded;
this is how I taught, and that is how my colleagues taught.
Is it not that he says, "It is from a tradition,"
and they say, "This is how it seems in our eyes"?

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן: כָּךְ דָּרַשְׁתִּי, וְכָךְ דָּרְשׁוּ חֲבֵירַי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After both opinions are stated, the גמרא tests them against the משנה's wording.
steps.raayaObject: רבי אלעזר's view (and against רב כהנא) that a זקן with a tradition is killed.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's wording: 'כך למדתי וכך למדו חבירי.'

steps.title: No, the משנה Means the זקן Uses Reasoning
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof: the משנה can mean the זקן speaks from his own reasoning while the court holds the tradition.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. He says 'this is how it seems to me,' and they say 'it is from tradition.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes aside the proof from the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'this is how I taught' do not have to mean the זקן has a tradition. The משנה can be talking about the case where everyone agrees he is killed: he uses reasoning and the court has the tradition. So the משנה fits רב כהנא too.

keyTerms.meaning: This is how it seems in my eyes, meaning my own reasoning

phrases.english: No, he says, "This is how it seems in my eyes,"
and they say it from a tradition.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 25.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof from the משנה's wording; neither opinion is proven or disproven.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the משנה's case is a זקן with a tradition, but it can be a זקן using reasoning against the court's tradition, which is רב כהנא's case of execution.

steps.title: רבי יאשיה's Three Teachings From זעירא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens another attempt at evidence: רבי יאשיה heard three teachings from זעירא of ירושלים, the first being that a husband who cancels his warning to his wife has canceled it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רבי יאשיה said: זעירא, one of the people of ירושלים, told me three things. A husband who canceled his warning to his wife, his warning is canceled.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new 'come and hear' to shed light on the question. It is setting up the next move, and only the first of the three teachings appears here; the rest continues after this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first teaching is about קינוי: a husband who warned his wife not to be alone with a certain man can take back the warning, and it is canceled. This first item is not yet the point that matters for the זקן ממרא; the גמרא is listing all three teachings before using them.

keyTerms.meaning: A husband's warning to his wife not to be alone with a certain man
Forgave, canceled

phrases.english: Come and hear, as Rabbi Yoshiya said:
Three things told me
Zeira, of the people of Jerusalem:
A husband who canceled his warning —
phrases.notes: This is the warning that a husband gives his wife (the סוטה case): don't be alone with that man.

phrases.english: his warning is canceled.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proof from the משנה was rejected, the גמרא brings a new source.
steps.raayaObject: The dispute about the זקן ממרא (the relevant part comes later in רבי יאשיה's list).
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יאשיה's report of three teachings from זעירא of ירושלים.
